html:
SMTO-PSM-0004 — This parameter's name clashes with a built-in @ option

GUID: 5e0acc39-31ca-41c7-9993-100aca5fcc7a
Slug: parameter-conflict
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • This saved parameter has a name SMTO uses for one of its built-in @ options. It shows Reference unavailable and can't be picked with @ until it's renamed. Its value hasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select the parameter marked Reference unavailable. That label marks the parameter whose name clashes.
  2. Select Rename parameter, type a name that isn't a built-in @ option in the Key field (for example add a word to it), and select Save. Once the name is different, SMTO can tell your parameter apart from its own @ options.
  3. From now on, mention the parameter by its new name with @. The old name always points to SMTO's built-in option, not to your parameter.

What success looks like

  • The Reference unavailable label disappears and Copy reference works again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Rename the original parameter rather than making a second copy, so its saved value stays in one place.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A stored parameter's normalized key matches a reserved @ palette namespace or action, so its metadata is flagged mention_conflict and @ references to it are ignored.

What this means

  • Parameter metadata projection finds an existing normalized key reserved by the mention palette and emits a conflict annotation. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter metadata projection finds an existing normalized key reserved by the mention palette and emits a conflict annotation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing key and mention_conflict annotation; the annotation itself does not delete or rename data.

How to fix it

  • Rename the Parameter Store key (Rename parameter in the Parameter Store page, or the store update API with a new key) to a value for which is_reserved() is false. parse_references skips reserved tokens, so the record cannot be referenced through @ until it is renamed.
  • Rename the Parameter Store key to avoid the built-in namespace before selecting it from the @ palette.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate supported rename gives the parameter an unambiguous palette identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
